Prove that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}}=\frac{1}{2}(1-\frac{1}{{3}^{n}})$ using mathematical induction.

We proceed using induction on $n.$

**Base Case**: We first prove that our statement is true for the base case $n=\,${{field-1}}.

For the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{1}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}}={{field-2}}\end{aligned}
$$

which equals the right-hand side. Thus, our statement is {{field-3}} for $n=1.$

**Inductive Hypothesis**: We assume that for some $n=$ {{field-4}}, we have

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{k}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \,{{field-5}}.
$$

**Inductive Step**: To prove $P(k+1),$ we write

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{k+1}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}}=({\sum }_{i=1}^{k}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}})+{{field-6}}.
$$

By the inductive hypothesis, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}({\sum }_{i=1}^{k}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}})+\frac{1}{{3}^{k+1}} & ={{field-7}} \\  & ={{field-8}},\end{aligned}
$$

as required.

Therefore, by the principle of induction, ${\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{{3}^{i}}=\frac{1}{2}(1-\frac{1}{{3}^{n}})$ is true for all {{field-9}}.
